To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the vector-meson-nucleon coupling constants are determined in a VMD framework, (ii) the in-medium properties are studied in the linear sigma model, (iii) the in-medium vector meson properties are determined by a fit to experimental data, (iv) the coupling constants and the in-medium vector-meson properties are used in a calculation of the decay width of the nucleon resonances.
the vector meson decay of baryon resonances is strongly influenced by in-medium modifications of the vector mesons.
the in-medium mass and decay width of the ρ meson increase with baryon density, while the in-medium mass of the ω meson decreases.

the vector mesons do couple to nucleon resonations, but that the strength of the coupling is not large enough to be of relevance in the present context of the in-medium modification of the vector meson masses.

the in-medium properties are not much affected by the coupling to nucleon resonaces.
the coupling of vector to nucleon resonant states is very small and that the in-medium modification of the vector meson mass is very moderate.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the vector meson decay of nucleon resonances is not a simple isospin-averaged process, but that the decay into the various vector mesons is strongly influenced by the isospin structure of the resonance itself.
the vector meson decay of nucleon resonances is a very sensitive probe of the vector meson properties in the nuclear medium.
